## The Collatz conjecture

The conjecture (unsolved) that repeating the following operation $T$ on a positive integer $n$ always reaches $1$, wherever it starts.

$$
T(n) = \begin{cases} n/2 & n \equiv 0 \pmod 2 \\ 3n+1 & n \equiv 1 \pmod 2 \end{cases}
$$

Make the sequence by the recurrence $a_0 = n$, $a_{k+1} = T(a_k)$, and count the smallest $k$ with $a_k = 1$ (the stopping time). For $n = 27$ it reaches $1$ in $111$ steps, with a maximum of $9232$ on the way.

- **collatz-cpp**, **collatz-py**, **collatz-jl**, **collatz-r**: the same loop written in C++, Python, Julia and R as Cards in Cards (go inside to edit). Julia and R Cards run in a separate process per invocation and remember nothing, so they pass the sequence so far on in the message. R handles values exactly only below $2^{53}$
- **compare**: checks that the four sequences agree
- **record**: writes the sequence to `collatz.csv` and keeps it as an artifact

Try changing the value of **initial**, and maxRuns (the limit on repetitions) of **check** inside.
